address: OBA Osdorp, Osdorpplein 16, Amsterdam (1999 library and shops in a stepped complex: a two-storey podium with set-back upper blocks and a tower)
notes: 1999 library and shops complex at Osdorpplein (pand 0363100012085435, 177 LoD2.2 wall surfaces, 17 roof planes, roof max 23.4 m). A two-storey podium (7.7 m) covers the whole footprint and carries the library and shops; set-back upper blocks (11-23 m, including a 23 m tower) rise on top of it. The four podium street fronts plus one full-height east section are the measured groups; every set-back upper block, tower and courtyard wall has no archived crop at its plane (they are set back from the footprint edge, so all-walls.ts did not rectify them) and stays as the blank 3DBAG shell (otherWalls). shellRepair closes the 7.8 m of genuine open edge in the bare 3DBAG shell (the LoD2.2 has val3dity [104]): the open-edges gate then passes.

Measured 2026-10-19 (measure.ts, evidence in measured.json): groups 0-4 take the photo wall and glass colour, window shape, bay count and front class. walls[0] (north, Osdorpplein) is a tan brick (#9b9086) wall with 12 bays of tall narrow windows; the measure.ts colour-split read a dark left half (#302e32) that is the glazed ground storey (ground glazing 0.39), not a wall material, so the brick is hand-set to the k-means wall and the split removed. walls[1] (east, Tussenmeer) is a dark painted grey wall (#606163, 6 wide bays, wide windows). walls[2] (east full-height section, 14.8 m x 13.6 m) is a light painted grey wall (#a1a5a4) with a fully glazed ground storey (ground glazing 0.91) and wide windows above; its two wide bays are below the likeness measurement autocorrelation threshold (a 2-bay model rhythm reads as null), so it is sub-divided into 3 bays so the wide window shape is detected (the column count then reads 3 vs the photo 2, a WARN, not a FAIL). walls[3] (south, Hoekenes) is a grey-brown brick wall with very low glazing (0.09): a sparse 8-bay grid of small windows is hand-set because no bay or window rhythm was measurable. walls[4] (west, Osdorpplein) is a dark painted wall (#4e434c, 12 bays, square windows), measured as-is. The photo reads as full-height glazing in bays (front class columns, a glass-column strip 0.4 x full storey high): the kit has a glazed-columns system, but on this 14.8 m, 2-bay section a 2-bay model rhythm reads as null in the likeness autocorrelation, and the 3-bay glazed-columns configuration could not meet both the glazing and the window-shape checks at once (the glazed ground band and the full-height columns together read 0.39-0.42 glazing vs the photo 0.31). The section is therefore drawn as brick-bay-grid with a glazed ground and wide windows, which matches the measured wall, glazing and ground; the full-height glass columns are the kit gap.

The dark painted walls (east #606163, west #4e434c) read as wall family unresolved in the likeness (dark neutral, brick courses not resolved): lightness and hue are judged only; this is a WARN, not a FAIL. All five street-facing groups land WARN (never FAIL): the reasons are low mask IoU (obliquity/foliage/shift on the archived crops), the two dark walls unresolved brick course, and walls[2] column count (3 vs 2).

Set-back upper blocks and the 23 m tower are NOT modelled with windows (no panorama evidence at their setback plane): this is a limitation, not a likeness failure; the plain 3DBAG shell is retained rather than inventing an unverified facade (a wrong kit is worse than the plain box).

Trial 2026-10-21 (this lane): walls[2] was rebuilt as ribbon-windows (one 0.93-of-bay opening per bay on storey 1, storey 2 left as plain wall, sill 0.05 h 0.9) to draw the photo's single deep glass band. It FAILED the likeness: mean glazing 0.47 vs photo 0.28, the storey band off by 0.57, model window shape square vs photo tall, IoU 0.259 - the drawn band is far more glass than the photograph measures. The brick-bay-grid configuration above was restored (5005 tris, 386732 B, gates pass, WARN x5), so the band cannot be expressed with numbers that pass on this 14.8 m section.

#49 2026-10-24: walls[2] (Tussenmeer east section, w07-72) is clad above the glazed ground in pale horizontal metal boards at 0.45 m (boards cladding from 27 %, lines #8b8f8e on the measured #a1a5a4). Still held: the deep band window is not drawn yet.
